newsitem.title: UK: Enron to proceed with Sutton Bridge power.
newsitem.headline: Enron to proceed with Sutton Bridge power.

text.p: Enron is to proceed with the proposed Sutton Bidge Power Station in Lincolnshire in Britain subject to regulatory approval, the company announced in a statement on Monday.
Enron will build and own the 300 million stg combined cycle gas turbine plant, which will employ approximately 50 people permanently once it starts commercial operations in mid 1999.
Enron has recently applied to the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to increase the plant's capacity by 90 MegaWatts to 790 MW. Planning permission for the original project was granted in 1992.
Enron has also entered into sales and purchase agreements covering both gas and power with Hanson Plc's Eastern Group and its subsidiary, Eastern Natural Gas.

Under the agreement, Eastern will buy up to 475 million therms of gas a year from Enron Capital and Trade Resources Ltd over 15 years from mid 1999. The price will relate to the prevailing market price for gas, and daily volumes will depend on the relative prices of gas and electricity at the time.
In this way, Eastern said in a statement that Enron will be providing risk management services to Eastern.

And as well as buying gas, Eastern will also sell gas to Enron at volumes related to an electricity purchase agreement under which Eastern will buy electricity from the Sutton Bridge plant. This time, Eastern said, it will be providing risk management services to Enron.
Enron Europe CEO Mark Frevert said "this project will allow Enron to expand significantly its presence and competitive position in both the UK electricity and gas markets."

And John Devaney, Executive Chairman of Eastern Group, said "these transactions illustrate both our capacity to innovate and sell energy risk management services as well as building more flexibility into our overall gas and electricity portfolios."
